title: Molten regolith electrolysis energy cost for oxygen
bottleneck: Molten regolith electrolysis could extract oxygen and metals directly from lunar soil by melting it above 1,600 C and passing current through it — no imported reagents needed. But melting rock is enormously energy-intensive, electrodes corrode in the molten bath, and containing 1,600 C liquid in a lunar plant that must run autonomously for years is a materials and reliability nightmare. The energy per kilogram of oxygen may exceed what a base can afford.
why_it_blocks: Oxygen is the largest-mass propellant component; if the most reagent-free extraction method is too power-hungry, ISRU oxygen stays dependent on scarcer water ice or imported chemistry.
current_state: Lab-scale demonstrations prove the chemistry; pilot-plant energy economics and electrode lifetime remain unproven. No lunar demonstration exists.
